notes: Any walk up a mountain, not only technical climbing. ハイキング suggests an easier outing.

examples.tl: 週末はよく登山をします。
examples.rom: Shūmatsu wa yoku tozan o shimasu.
examples.en: I often go hiking on weekends.

notes: Mt. Nantai's is inside Futarasan Shrine Chūgūshi by Lake Chuzenji: you sign in and pay there.

examples.tl: 男体山の登山口はどこですか。
examples.rom: Nantai-san no tozanguchi wa doko desu ka.
examples.en: Where is the trailhead for Mt. Nantai?

notes: 頂上 (chōjō) means the same and is a bit more everyday.

examples.tl: 山頂まであと1時間です。
examples.rom: Sanchō made ato ichijikan desu.
examples.en: One more hour to the summit.

notes: Hikers greet each other with こんにちは as they pass; those climbing have right of way.

examples.tl: 登山道は雨で滑りやすいです。
examples.rom: Tozandō wa ame de suberiyasui desu.
examples.en: The trail is slippery from the rain.

notes: In names usually read -san: 男体山 Nantai-san, 富士山 Fuji-san (never 'Fuji-yama').

examples.tl: あの山は男体山です。
examples.rom: Ano yama wa Nantai-san desu.
examples.en: That mountain is Mt. Nantai.

notes: Staffed huts on the big mountains sell meals and beds, cash only. 避難小屋 (hinangoya) = unstaffed emergency shelter.

examples.tl: 山小屋で水は買えますか。
examples.rom: Yamagoya de mizu wa kaemasu ka.
examples.en: Can I buy water at the mountain hut?

tl: 頂上までどのくらいかかりますか。
accept: How long does it take to the top?
How long does it take to the summit?
notes: Trail signs give times, not distances: 山頂まで90分 = 90 minutes to the summit.

examples.tl: 「頂上までどのくらいかかりますか。」「ここから2時間ぐらいです。」
examples.rom: Chōjō made donokurai kakarimasu ka. / Koko kara nijikan gurai desu.
examples.en: How long to the summit? / About two hours from here.

notes: Paid at the trailhead on some mountains. At Mt. Nantai's shrine gate it is called 登拝料 (tohairyō).

examples.tl: 入山料はいくらですか。
examples.rom: Nyūzanryō wa ikura desu ka.
examples.en: How much is the climbing fee?

notes: With します: 下山します = to go down. Set a turnaround time so you are down before dark.

examples.tl: 3時までに下山したいです。
examples.rom: Sanji made ni gezan shitai desu.
examples.en: I want to be down by three.

tl: 天気が悪くなりそうです。
en: The weather is about to turn bad.
accept: The weather looks like it's getting worse
It looks like the weather will get worse
The weather looks like turning bad
The weather is about to turn
notes: 〜そうです after a verb stem = it looks like it will. 雨が降りそうです = it looks like rain.

examples.tl: 天気が悪くなりそうですから、下山しましょう。
examples.rom: Tenki ga waruku narisō desu kara, gezan shimashō.
examples.en: The weather looks like turning, so let's head down.

notes: Covers thunder and lightning. Nikko is known for summer afternoon storms: start early, be off the top by midday.

examples.tl: 午後は雷に注意してください。
examples.rom: Gogo wa kaminari ni chūi shite kudasai.
examples.en: Watch out for thunderstorms in the afternoon.

notes: Black bears live around Nikko. Signs read 熊出没注意; hikers carry a bear bell (熊鈴 kumasuzu).

examples.tl: この山に熊はいますか。
examples.rom: Kono yama ni kuma wa imasu ka.
examples.en: Are there bears on this mountain?

notes: Literally 'my throat has dried'.

examples.tl: のどが渇きました。水はまだありますか。
examples.rom: Nodo ga kawakimashita. Mizu wa mada arimasu ka.
examples.en: I'm thirsty. Is there still some water?

notes: Past form in Japanese: 'I have become tired'.

examples.tl: 疲れました。少し休みましょう。
examples.rom: Tsukaremashita. Sukoshi yasumimashō.
examples.en: I'm tired. Let's rest a little.

notes: 湿布 (shippu), medicated cooling patches from any drugstore, are the local cure.

examples.tl: 昨日の登山で足が筋肉痛です。
examples.rom: Kinō no tozan de ashi ga kinnikutsū desu.
examples.en: My legs are sore from yesterday's hike.

notes: 休憩所 (kyūkeijo) = rest area.

examples.tl: ここで10分休憩しましょう。
examples.rom: Koko de juppun kyūkei shimashō.
examples.en: Let's take a ten-minute break here.

notes: Plain form: 走る (hashiru). ランニング (ranningu) and ジョギング (jogingu) are the nouns.

examples.tl: 毎朝、5キロ走ります。
examples.rom: Maiasa, go-kiro hashirimasu.
examples.en: I run 5 km every morning.

notes: Loosely used for any road race. ハーフマラソン = half, フルマラソン = the full distance.

examples.tl: 来年、東京マラソンを走りたいです。
examples.rom: Rainen, Tōkyō Marason o hashiritai desu.
examples.en: I want to run the Tokyo Marathon next year.

notes: The usual word for an organized race: マラソン大会. Signing up is エントリー (entorī).

examples.tl: 日曜日にマラソン大会に出ます。
examples.rom: Nichiyōbi ni marason taikai ni demasu.
examples.en: I'm running in a race on Sunday.

notes: The finish, not a target. スタート (sutāto) = start. ゴールしました = I finished.

examples.tl: ゴールまであと2キロです。
examples.rom: Gōru made ato ni-kiro desu.
examples.en: Two more kilometers to the finish.

notes: Collected at 受付 with your entry confirmation, often the day before. Also called ナンバーカード.

examples.tl: ゼッケンはどこでもらえますか。
examples.rom: Zekken wa doko de moraemasu ka.
examples.en: Where do I pick up my bib?

notes: Any sign-in desk: races, trailhead registration, clinics, museums. You see it on signs everywhere.

examples.tl: 受付は何時からですか。
examples.rom: Uketsuke wa nanji kara desu ka.
examples.en: What time does registration open?

notes: On race courses. エイド (eido) = an aid station that also has food.

examples.tl: 次の給水所はどこですか。
examples.rom: Tsugi no kyūsuijo wa doko desu ka.
examples.en: Where is the next water station?

notes: Public sports centers sell cheap one-visit tickets. Indoor-only shoes are required.

examples.tl: ホテルにジムはありますか。
examples.rom: Hoteru ni jimu wa arimasu ka.
examples.en: Is there a gym in the hotel?

notes: Shouted along race courses and on trails. Reply 頑張ります (ganbarimasu) = I'll do my best.

examples.tl: 「明日、ハーフマラソンを走ります。」「頑張ってください！」
examples.rom: Ashita, hāfu marason o hashirimasu. / Ganbatte kudasai!
examples.en: I'm running a half marathon tomorrow. / Good luck!

notes: Trails are split into ten stages, 一合目 (ichigōme) up to 九合目 (kyūgōme), then the summit.

examples.tl: 今、五合目です。あと半分です。
examples.rom: Ima, gogōme desu. Ato hanbun desu.
examples.en: We're at the fifth station now. Half to go.

tl: 最終バスは何時ですか。
rom: Saishū basu wa nanji desu ka.
en: What time is the last bus?
accept: What time does the last bus leave?
notes: Check before you start up: buses from mountain areas can stop early in the evening.

examples.tl: 東武日光駅行きの最終バスは何時ですか。
examples.rom: Tōbu-Nikkō-eki yuki no saishū basu wa nanji desu ka.
examples.en: What time is the last bus to Tobu-Nikko Station?

tl: この道で合っていますか。
rom: Kono michi de atte imasu ka.
accept: Am I on the right path?

examples.tl: 山頂はこの道で合っていますか。
examples.rom: Sanchō wa kono michi de atte imasu ka.
examples.en: Is this the right way to the summit?

notes: Step aside and say it to let faster hikers pass, or at a doorway or elevator.

examples.tl: 「お先にどうぞ。」「ありがとうございます。」
examples.rom: Osaki ni dōzo. / Arigatō gozaimasu.
examples.en: After you. / Thank you.
